territorial_scope.description: Applies within the State of Illinois; frontier-model development, deployment or operation in whole or in part in the State triggers the disclosure filing duty.

evidence.quote: in whole or in part in this State

summary.short: Illinois statute regulating developers of frontier AI models (trained above 10^26 operations). Imposes safety-framework, transparency, third-party audit, incident-reporting and whistleblower duties, plus a state disclosure filing, from 1 January 2027 with some duties from 2028.
summary.long: The Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act defines a frontier model as a foundation model trained with more than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations, and a large frontier developer as a frontier developer whose affiliates collectively had gross revenues above $500,000,000 in the preceding calendar year. From 1 January 2027, a large frontier developer may not develop, deploy or operate a frontier model in whole or in part in Illinois without a current disclosure statement filed with the Illinois Emergency Management Agency and Office of Homeland Security and paying the required fee (Section 18). From 1 January 2028, large frontier developers must write, implement and publish a frontier AI framework, review it at least annually, and retain an annual independent third-party audit (Section 10). Frontier developers must publish a transparency report before or concurrently with deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model (Section 10(c)). Frontier developers must report critical safety incidents within 72 hours, or within 24 hours for an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury (Section 15(c)). The Act protects covered employees who disclose information about catastrophic risk or violations of the Act, and requires large frontier developers to offer an anonymous internal disclosure process (Section 20). Interoperability with designated federal standards can serve as a declared compliance route (Section 17). The Attorney General brings civil actions for civil penalties of up to $1,000,000 per first violation and $3,000,000 per subsequent violation (Section 25). The Act creates no private right of action.

notes: Section 80 reproduces Freedom of Information Act Section 7.5 in three versions (before amendment, after P.A. 104-457, after P.A. 104-441) with differing lettering and dates; all three are coded as presented, not as one consolidated text. The version after P.A. 104-441 contains a duplicated letter label '(vvv) (uuu)'. Section 17 refers to federal laws, regulations or guidance without naming them. Section 18(a) disclosure filing starts January 1, 2027 (same date as Section 99 effective date), while Section 10 duties start January 1, 2028. Section 25(d) states that no private right of action arises from violations of this Act; the text does not address private rights under the amended Whistleblower Act.

thresholds.conditions: Harm must be materially contributed to by the frontier model's development, storage, use or deployment and arise from one of the three listed conduct types (CBRN expert assistance, unsupervised cyberattack or equivalent crime, evading control); listed exclusions do not count.

thresholds.variable_text: computing power used to train a foundation model
thresholds.value_text: greater than 10²⁶ integer or floating-point operations
thresholds.measurement: computing power for the original training run plus any subsequent fine-tuning, reinforcement learning or other material modifications the developer applies to a preceding foundation model
thresholds.consequence: A foundation model above this value is a frontier model, and a person training it is a frontier developer under the Act.
thresholds.conditions: The model must be a foundation model: trained on a broad data set, designed for generality of output and adaptable to a wide range of distinctive tasks.

evidence.quote: trained using a quantity of computing power greater than 10²⁶ integer or floating-point operations

thresholds.measurement: annual gross revenues collectively of the frontier developer and its affiliates in the preceding calendar year
thresholds.consequence: A frontier developer above this level is a large frontier developer, with additional duties in Sections 10, 15, 18 and 20.
thresholds.conditions: The person must also be a frontier developer (trains or initiates training of a frontier model); affiliate revenues are aggregated.
